crime: Every evening, a girl climbed alone to the fork of the courtyard tree to watch the stars, and {WITCH_NAME} waited at its foot. Whenever she tried to follow, she fell off the first branch. She could only climb if someone told her how.
One night the girl dropped her blanket down to her. "It's yours now."
Years ago, her mother had given her the coat off her own back with the same words. The next morning, her mother left her at the door of a children's home.
{WITCH_NAME} called up into the branches. "Tell me to come up."

"Come up," the girl called, and the instant she said it, {WITCH_NAME}'s hands and feet found every hold and carried her flawlessly to the fork. There she pushed the girl off. The girl struck the stone rim of the fountain below.
With no one left to tell her how, she started down, slipped and fell, tearing her palms raw. She ran inside crying, "She fell!"

In the trial court, the prisoners settled on what had happened: the girl had fallen from the fork alone, and {WITCH_NAME} had torn her palms trying to climb up to her. Then one prisoner spoke up. The morning after the fall, from the upper railing, she had seen a strip of {WITCH_NAME}'s sleeve snagged in the fork, high above the first branch.
The prisoners understood. The girl had called her up, and {WITCH_NAME} had been right beside her when she fell.
fields.epitaph: The blanket was never a goodbye; it was for all the nights she meant to stay.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Heard Goodbye in Every Gift
execution: The execution stand raises a tall, bare tree, its fork heaped with folded blankets. She is bound sitting among the roots at its foot. The tree tips its blankets down one after another, each unfolding over her as it falls. She paws clumsily at the folds over her face. No one calls a single word to her. The tree lets its last blanket settle on the still mound, and the fork stands empty.

magic.name: Say the Word
magic.text: The moment someone tells her to do something, she does it perfectly.
